correctness.rationale: DB_w=ζ^(−1)B_wD and primitive order q make all interior Gaussian binomial coefficients vanish (nonzero denominators), so T^q=a^qI+B_w^q. Every length-q weight product is W; rearranging indices by residue gives the isometric q-fold sum of A=αI+WB, α=a^q. A first-coordinate-normalized eigenvector of T has q-step ratio (λ^q−α)/W; it belongs to ℓ^p exactly when that ratio has modulus <1, including ratio zero. Spectral mapping gives the closed lemniscate upper inclusion and openness of λ↦λ^q gives closure of the strict lemniscate, proving the reverse inclusion. The recursive diagonal gauge is bounded with bounded inverse iff its per-period modulus is one; different R give different spectra and exclude even nondiagonal similarity with the stated parameters fixed. For R>L the eigenvalue disk of A crosses the unit circle. The geometric eigenvectors (z^k)_{k≥0} have dense span on any subset accumulating inside |z|<1, by analytic annihilators; use each summand separately. The inside and outside spans give mixing by adding decaying preimages of finite outside-eigenvector sums to a finite inside-eigenvector sum. A closed circle subarc in the disk supplies an atomless arclength measure meeting Grivaux Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.4 (arXiv:1001.2026, pp. 2–3), and roots of unity supply a dense periodic span. Mixing passes from T^q to T by applying it to (T^r)^−1 of each target open set, which is nonempty because T^q has dense range. Return times for T^q yield positive lower densities after dilation by q for T. If R≤L, then either c≤1 and A has norm ≤1, so the whole orbit is bounded, or c≥1 and A is invertible with inverse norm ≤1, so a nonzero orbit is bounded away from zero on all q residue classes. For shadowing, the hypotheses of Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7 of arXiv:2610.15023 are met; the periodic ratio geometric means coincide at (|λ^q−α|/R)^(1/q), whose numerator sweeps [L,U] on the unit circle. Independently recover the same thresholds: forward shadowing is equivalent for T and T^q by sampling every q steps in one direction (the accumulated error is at most δ∑_{r<q}||T^r||) and filling the gaps by exact iterates in the other. It is equivalent on the finite coordinate sum and on A by coordinate projections and choosing coordinate accuracies. If R<L, A or A^−1 is a strict contraction. If R>U, the forward shift S gives the strict-contraction right inverse C=(1/W)S(I+(α/W)S)^−1, ||C||≤1/(R−c). For a bounded error e_n in x_{n+1}=Ax_n+e_n, solve d_{n+1}=Ad_n+e_n by forward convolution when ||A||<1, or by d_n=−∑_{j≥0}C^(j+1)e_{n+j} with a contracting right inverse (including the A^−1 case). If L≤R≤U, choose λ=α+Wz with |λ|=|z|=1. In the linear dual, normalized finite coefficient lists z^(−(j−1))t_j with triangular tapers of length 2M give ||(A'−λ)φ_M||=O(M^−1): the residual is the first difference of the taper, also for dual ℓ^∞ at p=1. Shadowing with tracing error 1 would solve the difference equation for all sufficiently small errors. Take e_n=δλ^(n+1)v with ||v||≤1 and Re φ_M(v)≥1/2. If ||d_n||≤1, Re φ_M(λ^(−n)d_n) increases each step by at least δ/2−||(A'−λ)φ_M||>0 for large M, a contradiction. This includes both equality boundaries. At a=0 the mixed interval is empty (not a singleton); at a=1 L=0 and U=2. originality.rationale: Credit attaches to the use of the exact cyclotomic reduction to classify similarity, spectra and the sharp simultaneous linear-dynamics threshold in the frozen family. residual_risks: The 2003 primary full text was unavailable in the lawful copies attempted. An older treatment of cyclic triangular operators may subsume the spectral or dynamical classification.

value.rationale: The complete product-modulus invariant and sharp regimes simplify a natural nonconstant diagonal-plus-shift family. Individual weights can vary without changing the similarity or dynamical behavior, and the phase diagram distinguishes frequently hypercyclic and mixing examples with versus without shadowing, including precise boundary failures. The contribution is the reduction and resulting sharp classification, not a new general shadowing theorem or evidence from finite matrix sections.
